name: Fazilka–Askot Highway
aka: Formed from parts of the former NH 10, NH 24, NH 87, NH 74 and NH 125
history: NH 9 crosses north India from Fazilka near the Pakistan border to Askot high in the Kumaon hills near Nepal. It was created in the 2010 renumbering by joining parts of five older highways, including the old NH 10 (Delhi–Hisar–Sirsa) and the old NH 24 (Delhi–Moradabad). West of Delhi it runs through the farm towns of Haryana; east of Delhi it crosses the Ganga plains, and after Tanakpur it climbs through Champawat and Pithoragarh into the mountains.
facts: Runs from near India's border with Pakistan (Fazilka) to the hills close to its border with Nepal (Askot).
Its Delhi–Ghaziabad stretch is shared with the Delhi–Meerut Expressway and is one of India's widest roads, up to about 14 lanes.
Crosses the river Ganga at Garhmukteshwar.
The Tanakpur–Pithoragarh hill section lies on the traditional pilgrim route towards Kailash–Mansarovar.
Five old highway numbers (NH 10, 24, 87, 74 and 125) were stitched together to form it.
